fix.note: Official permission/permit; 허가(를) 받다. Personal permission (parents) is 허락.

ex.en: You need permission to take pictures here.

ex.s: 이 건물은 허가 없이 못 들어가요.
ex.en: You can't enter this building without permission.
We finally got a business permit for the store.
The visa application process is complicated.
Please tell me the refund procedure.
What's the admission process?
The letters are too small for me to see.
I memorized all the Hangul letters.
The lettering on the sign is so pretty.

ex.s: 선생님이 이 부분을 여러 번 강조하셨어요.
ex.en: The teacher emphasized this part several times.
The doctor stressed exercise.
The team leader stressed the deadline.
I'll pray that you do well on your test.
Grandma prays every morning.
We prayed for the surgery to go well.
Look over the lease carefully.
The doctor examined my throat.
I'm slowly looking around the store.

fix.note: Job title: 김 대리님. 대리(운전) = designated-driver service.

ex.en: Assistant Manager Park is in a meeting right now.
My husband was promoted to assistant manager this year.
We've been drinking, so let's call a designated driver.

fix.note: Often 천사 같다 = angelic, so kind.

ex.s: 우리 아기는 잘 때 천사 같아요.
ex.en: Our baby looks like an angel when she sleeps.
Thanks for helping. You're a real angel.
That nurse was a real angel.
Open your books to page 30.
We spread out a mat in the park and sat down.
We unfolded the map and found the way.

fix.en: to be ahead; to come before

ex.s: 우리 팀이 이 대 일로 앞서고 있어요.
ex.en: Our team is leading 2 to 1.
Mom walked on ahead.
Before the meeting, let me briefly say hello.

ex.s: 이 상자 좀 같이 들어 줄래요?
ex.en: Could you help me lift this box?
I put the gift in a pretty box.
I bought a box at the post office.
I found my passport right before leaving.
It's right before the exam, so I'm really nervous.
Don't look at your phone right before bed.

notes: Fixes: 허가 vs 허락 (parental permission is 허락), unnatural 입원 절차는 어디서 해요, redundant 문자 글자.
